_file_header.weight_derivation_note: Hallmark link weights in companion compound file are derived from evidence_strength + human_evidence; biomarker thresholds here use clinical_consensus where no single PMID supports a numeric cutoff.
_file_header.weight_rationale: Equal weights applied. Lopez-Otin 2013 (PMID 23746838) and 2023 (PMID 36599349) present hallmarks as interconnected without quantitative ranking. No published systematic review assigns differential weights. Nature 2022 critical review (PMID 35880523) notes hallmarks are defined phenomenologically, not quantitatively.
_file_header.weight_source: absence of evidence for differential weighting

grimage_components.description: GrimAge: DNAm surrogates for 7 plasma proteins plus DNAm pack-years

_file_header.phenoage_note: Clinical PhenoAge / phenotypic age (Levine 2018, PMID 29676998, Table 1 Gompertz weights) uses albumin, creatinine, glucose, CRP (log), lymphocyte%, MCV, RDW, alkaline phosphatase, WBC + chronological age — not GGT. CRP enters as log(CRP) continuously; it does not define an optimal 0.5 mg/L threshold.

Elevated LDL drives atherogenic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction.
LDL-C reflects lipid metabolism and nutrient-sensing pathway activity.
Low HDL is associated with increased cardiovascular inflammation and impaired reverse cholesterol transport.
HDL particles carry antioxidant enzymes; low HDL correlates with mitochondrial oxidative stress.
Elevated triglycerides reflect deregulated lipid/nutrient-sensing pathways including insulin resistance.
Hypertriglyceridemia promotes pro-inflammatory signaling and endothelial dysfunction.
AST elevation reflects hepatic mitochondrial stress and oxidative damage.
Chronic liver injury and elevated AST are associated with hepatocyte senescence accumulation.
ALT elevation is a sensitive marker of hepatocyte mitochondrial and metabolic stress.
Chronic hepatic injury drives senescent cell accumulation and SASP-mediated inflammation.
ALT tracks metabolic liver disease and nutrient-sensing dysregulation in NAFLD/MASLD.
Thyroid hormone regulates mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation; TSH extremes reflect thyroid-mitochondrial axis disruption.
TSH and thyroid hormones modulate metabolic rate and nutrient utilization pathways.
Free T3 is the active thyroid hormone driving mitochondrial biogenesis and ATP production; low levels impair mitochondrial function.
T3 modulates metabolic rate and nutrient-sensing pathways including glucose and lipid metabolism.
Chronic cortisol excess accelerates cellular senescence via glucocorticoid receptor-mediated stress pathways.
Elevated cortisol drives systemic immunosuppression and disrupts cytokine signaling networks.
Glucocorticoid excess induces epigenetic reprogramming of stress-response genes.

Uric acid is the end product of purine catabolism; elevated levels reflect mitochondrial oxidative stress and xanthine oxidase activity.
Adiponectin activates AMPK and improves insulin sensitivity; low levels indicate nutrient-sensing dysregulation.
Adiponectin is an anti-inflammatory adipokine; low levels promote pro-inflammatory intercellular signaling.
Low adiponectin is associated with elevated inflammatory markers and metabolic syndrome.
SHBG is inversely regulated by insulin; low SHBG reflects insulin resistance and nutrient-sensing dysregulation.
SHBG levels modulate bioavailable sex hormones that influence tissue maintenance and senescence programs.

biomarkers.display_name: Omega-3 Index (EPA+DHA % of RBC fatty acids)

Klotho expression is regulated by epigenetic mechanisms; low klotho reflects epigenetic silencing in aging.
BDNF is a key neurotrophic factor mediating intercellular communication in the brain and periphery; low levels impair neuroplasticity.
Declining BDNF is associated with neuronal senescence and cognitive aging.
Low microbiome diversity is the defining feature of gut dysbiosis, associated with aging and disease.
Microbiome diversity influences gut-immune axis and systemic intercellular signaling via metabolites.
Low microbiome diversity is associated with increased intestinal permeability and systemic inflammation.
Taurine supports mitochondrial function and reduces mitochondrial ROS; taurine deficiency accelerates mitochondrial aging.
Taurine supplementation reduces senescence markers in multiple tissues; plasma taurine declines with age.
Taurine modulates nutrient-sensing pathways including mTOR and AMPK in aging tissues.
